+**No full pinned Debian13 A04 ELF differential has yet executed on the A01 kernel. The capability probe below is separate evidence and is not a full compatibility claim.** Linux host reference now has **31/32 pass**, with
+Rust/Tokio `not_run` because managed-host pathname AF_UNIX returns `EPERM`
+after its reviewed locked build; its four C ELF have a reproducible 28-case
+no-Python guest harness. A01 independently booted
+the real pinned Asterinas kernel in QEMU in [PR #5](https://github.com/TrillionniumFoundation/trillionnium-os-desktop/pull/5),
+including retained kernel/initramfs/serial. Those A01 smoke results are not an
+A04 guest pass. A04's new initramfs overlay/parser has been tested with
+synthetic input, but **not** booted in QEMU here (no QEMU/firmware/toolchain).
+
+The fixed Hepta source has now produced a temporary Agentd ELF through the real
+e2e dependency build: SHA-256
+`0a8266635f8dd1b49d5213af4f01aab6c66d7450d9b9e940f71490893ce404ae`, loader
+`/lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2`, with direct NEEDED entries for libc, libm,
+libgcc_s, libssl and libcrypto. The runtime test itself failed before a
+provider request: Wiremock matched zero Responses requests and no terminal
+receipt was emitted. `strace` was blocked by `PTRACE_TRACEME=EPERM`, so the
+full dynamic path, NSS/TLS/SQLite file closure and tool-effect trace remain
+unqualified. Missing host assembly or ptrace permission is not an OS bug.

+When a guest case fails, attach its Linux JSON reference, guest JSON evidence,
+exact ELF + rootfs SHA, QEMU boot serial/raw exit, syscall errno and minimal

+system service, Hepta host configuration, or unavailable credentials.

+### Fixed-commit Hepta composition boundary (source evidence, not an ABI bug)
+
+`codex-rs/hepta-agentd/src/main.rs:112-183` installs the explicitly requested
+`AgentdIntelligenceProductRunnerV1` via `with_intelligence_product_runner`,
+but has **no call** to `with_intelligence_invocation_provider`. The latter API
+exists (`config.rs:515-535`), is optional by default (`config.rs:217`), and
+`runtime.rs:80-119` only attaches it if a composition owner supplied one.
+This does **not** prove the provider can never be installed from a different
+host; it proves the standalone CLI flags inspected are insufficient for a
+canonical seven-owner ObjectiveStart demonstration. A07 must identify and
+verify the real product host composition and run/effect receipts. This is
+userland assembly evidence, not a reason to patch `kernel/asterinas/**`.
+

+## Follow-up: measured Linux syscall dependencies (2026-10-16)
+
+`tests/workloads/linux/baselines/linux-debian13-x86_64-ptrace.json` is an
+**actual PTRACE_GET_SYSCALL_INFO observation** for the 28 pinned C ELF cases
+with an identical staged loader/rootfs. The session observed 62 unique x86_64
+syscall numbers and 28/28 matching application facts. This inventory describes
+the *small selected probe workload*, **not** the required syscall completeness
+of Hepta, and **not** an A05/A06 kernel defect list.
+
+- A05 loader/VFS/storage: `arch_prctl`, `mmap`, `mprotect`, `munmap`, `openat`,
+  `newfstatat`, `pread64`, `pwrite64`, `fcntl`, `flock`, `fsync`, `fdatasync`,
+  `rename`, `unlink`, `msync`, `ftruncate` were all actually observed.
+- A05 IPC/process: `clone`, `wait4`, `sendmsg`, `recvmsg`, `socketpair`,
+  `shutdown`, `epoll_create1`, `epoll_ctl`, `epoll_wait`, `eventfd2`,
+  `timerfd_create`, `timerfd_settime`, `pipe2` were actually observed.
+- A06 scheduler/synchronization: `futex`, `set_tid_address`, `set_robust_list`,
+  `rseq`, `clock_nanosleep`, signal mask/return, `clone3` attempt and thread
+  exits. Internal `wait4` restart (`-ERESTARTSYS=512`) is NOT errno=512.
+
+The real reference has both expected failure errno and successes. Comparing
+only syscall names or total calls is insufficient: require exact C probe JSON
+invariants and check permissible race outcomes (no exact trace order). For each
+new-kernel failure, preserve actual QEMU serial and ABI output before deciding
+whether to ask A05/A06 for a kernel correction. A01 PR #5 contains accepted
+boot bytes but cannot stand in for this A04 guest run. The one-command
+`replay_qemu.py` was actually preflighted with missing QEMU and correctly
+returned **blocked**, not kernel failure; 32 host unit/integration regression tests
+passed. Real QEMU/Asterinas 28-case differential remains pending.
+
+## Newly closed host-only blocker: real extractable rootfs and chroot ELF tests
+
+A04's old deterministic rootfs tar had a **real USTAR bug**: the directory
+names contained trailing `/` but their type flags were `REGTYPE`, so extracting
+with Python's `tarfile` failed at `etc/` (`NotADirectoryError`). The corrected
+`capture.py` explicitly sets `DIRTYPE` and validates every file and directory
+against the existing 17-file manifest before fresh extraction. Old tar SHA
+`7ee7becc...` must no longer be used as an extractable image; replacement SHA
+`8c7522ac9a7aed75b7a27d73c8ba71dfd1baf875912b9bf47fcc6effe2d9c746`.
+
+**Actual Linux host tests:** pinned 28 C ELF cases execute under chroot with
+UID/GID 65534; all 28 return baseline-matching JSON with zero failures.
+The 17-file tar checks reject traversal/symlink and preserve read-only modes.
+This eliminates an A04 packaging problem, but is **not evidence of an A05/A06
+kernel bug** and not a substitute for the A01 Asterinas guest replay. The
+available A04 execution container still lacks QEMU/SeaBIOS, Rust/Cargo and
+full Hepta host assembly; guest and W1 remain not executed.
+

+## A04 bounded process cleanup and strict host evidence (2026-10-16)
+
+Original Linux only: `chroot_replay.py` and `chroot_stress.py` now share the
+**same bounded process-group and inherited-pipe cleanup**. The previous stress
+runner could call `communicate()` without a timeout after killing a timed-out
+parent, which could hang if a descendant escaped its process group. A detached
+child retaining stdout now produces `incomplete_descendant_cleanup` rather
+than a false passing case; it cannot establish full process-tree isolation.
+Both runners reject correct-looking JSON accompanied by stderr, extra stdout,
+duplicate JSON keys or non-finite numbers. These are test safety regressions,
+not evidence of a new-kernel syscall defect.
+
+Actual Debian 13 host validation: **62/62** Python unittests, **62/62** under
+`python3 -O`, **28/28** original-Linux chroot C ELF cases plus four not-run
+Python/Tokio cases, and **90/90** five-round chroot stress executions (18
+cases per round). The fixed 17-file USTAR SHA-256 remains
+`df8df2e3cdcd308ef62a59268a4519e2923c9ff78145e46f26a4092725e80797`.
+See `tests/workloads/linux/baselines/chroot-executor-hardening-20261016.json`
+for actual command/manifest/result log hashes and limitations. The A00 runner
+request remains [Issue #46](https://github.com/TrillionniumFoundation/trillionnium-os-desktop/issues/46).
+**Asterinas A04 ELF guest run, Rust/Tokio and real Hepta W1 remain unexecuted.**

+## A04 acceptance-chain hardening and cross-Agent guest evidence (2026-10-16)
+
+A04 branch synced to current `main` by merge commit
+`b58ab5bacf8cf160f778a5f5e7e098f37de5f1a3`: the merge tree was checked
+against main for every **non-A04** path (zero differences). The branch retains
+all 49 owned files. Root `README.md` remains 0 bytes.
+
+**Original-Linux reference false positives, reproduced then fixed:** the former
+`run.py` classified real child processes as passing even if they printed
+`{"ok":false,"ok":true}`, `{"ok":true,"rate":NaN}`, or a correct-looking
+JSON object with an error on stderr. Those are not an independent Linux
+behavioral reference. `run_case()` now requires **one unambiguous JSON line**, a
+strict true success fact, empty stderr and exit=0; it reports invalid output
+or timeout as failure without disclosing raw stderr. Six actual child-process
+negative/positive regressions are in `test_run_observation.py`. Real Linux
+baseline is unchanged: 31 passing cases, one missing Tokio case; all 31
+results match the byte-pinned Linux reference.
+
+**A01 QEMU executable identity:** previously the A04 runner accepted any
+executable emitting a plausible `QEMU emulator version ...` string, and could
+therefore be fooled by a fake emulator/serial producer. It now also pins the
+**actual executable bytes** to the A01 accepted QEMU SHA-256
+`8a35ccba41582fc6c38b9df85fc9e35fa1d42f414d2d7d8090ee9b2f5e7c0854`
+and checks again just before launch. A different distribution build must be
+independently reviewed, never silently promoted. This SHA check covers QEMU's
+main executable, **not** the full dynamic-library environment or guest
+attestation. The synthetic executable-spoof rejection is a host test, not a
+QEMU guest run.
+

+**28/28**, and chroot stress **90/90** (five rounds). These remain distinct
+from S1 storage crash durability and authenticated Hepta
+Agentd→App Server→actual tool execution, both unverified. See

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Compare identical ELF/input Linux-host and candidate-kernel JSON reports.
+
+Concurrent scheduling is not compared. Each workload reports observable
+invariants (row sets, join counts, locks, EOF, errno, release) instead.
+Never turn absent, errored or not-run tests into passing cases.
+"""
+import argparse
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+import sys
+
+
+def compare(reference, candidate, *, proven_only=False):
+    differences = []
+    blocked = []
+    matched = []
+    refs = reference.get("binaries", {})
+    cands = candidate.get("binaries", {})
+    for name, artifact in refs.items():
+        other = cands.get(name)
+        if not other:
+            blocked.append({"case": name, "reason": "missing ELF in candidate report"})
+        elif artifact.get("sha256") != other.get("sha256"):
+            differences.append({"case": name, "reason": "ELF bytes changed; not a differential test",
+                                "expected_sha256": artifact.get("sha256"), "actual_sha256": other.get("sha256")})
+        elif artifact.get("interpreter") != other.get("interpreter"):
+            differences.append({"case": name, "reason": "loader path changed"})
+    for name, baseline in reference.get("cases", {}).items():
+        observed = candidate.get("cases", {}).get(name)
+        if baseline.get("status") != "pass":
+            if not proven_only:
+                blocked.append({"case": name, "reason": "Linux reference did not run/pass"})
+            continue
+        if observed is None or observed.get("status") == "not_run":
+            blocked.append({"case": name, "reason": "candidate not run"})
+        elif observed.get("status") != "pass":
+            differences.append({"case": name, "reason": "candidate failed", "observed": observed})
+        elif baseline.get("exit_code") != observed.get("exit_code"):
+            differences.append({"case": name, "reason": "exit code differs",
+                                "expected": baseline.get("exit_code"), "actual": observed.get("exit_code")})
+        elif baseline.get("facts") != observed.get("facts"):
+            differences.append({"case": name, "reason": "observable behavior differs",
+                                "expected": baseline.get("facts"), "actual": observed.get("facts")})
+        else:
+            matched.append(name)
+    unknown = sorted(set(candidate.get("cases", {})) - set(reference.get("cases", {})))
+    for name in unknown:
+        blocked.append({"case": name, "reason": "no pinned Linux reference"})
+    guest_claim = candidate.get("suite") == "a04-linux-guest-differential"
+    guest_evidence = candidate.get("boot_evidence", {})
+    boot_verified = bool(guest_claim and candidate.get("guest_execution_verified") is True
+                         and guest_evidence.get("a01_kernel_elf_sha256_matches") is True
+                         and guest_evidence.get("a04_initramfs_sha256_matches") is True
+                         and guest_evidence.get("qemu_exit_code") == 33)
+    if guest_claim and not boot_verified:
+        blocked.append({"case": "kernel_boot", "reason": "missing valid guest/QEMU boot evidence"})
+    verdict = "fail" if differences else "incomplete" if blocked else (
+        "partial_match" if proven_only else "match")
+    return {"schema": 1, "verdict": verdict, "matched": matched,
+            "matched_count": len(matched), "differences": differences,
+            "blocked": blocked, "reference_case_count": len(reference.get("cases", {})),
+            "candidate_case_count": len(candidate.get("cases", {})),
+            "kernel_boot_verified": boot_verified,
+            "guest_compatibility_passed": candidate.get("guest_compatibility_passed") is True}
+
+
+def main():
+    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
+    ap.add_argument("--reference", type=Path, required=True)
+    ap.add_argument("--candidate", type=Path, required=True)
+    ap.add_argument("--output", type=Path, required=True)
+    ap.add_argument("--proven-only", action="store_true", help="compare only Linux-passed cases, mark partial_match")
+    args = ap.parse_args()
+    verdict = compare(json.loads(args.reference.read_text()),
+                      json.loads(args.candidate.read_text()), proven_only=args.proven_only)
+    args.output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    args.output.write_text(json.dumps(verdict, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
+    print(json.dumps({k: verdict[k] for k in ("verdict", "matched_count", "reference_case_count",
+                                               "candidate_case_count")}))
+    return 1 if verdict["verdict"] == "fail" else 2 if verdict["verdict"] == "incomplete" else 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main())

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Capture a REAL pinned Hepta Agentd run without touching production state.
+# Trace contents may contain private arguments, file paths and credentials.
+set -euo pipefail
+if (( $# < 2 )); then
+  echo 'usage: A04_EXPECTED_HEPTA_SHA256=<64hex> trace-hepta.sh /absolute/path/to/codex-hepta-agentd NEW_PRIVATE_OUTPUT_DIR [agentd flags...]' >&2
+  exit 64
+fi
+binary="$1"; out="$2"; shift 2
+if [[ "$binary" != /* || ! -f "$binary" || ! -x "$binary" ]]; then
+  echo 'absolute path to executable fixed-commit Hepta binary required' >&2
+  exit 66
+fi
+if [[ -e "$out" || -L "$out" ]]; then
+  echo 'output directory exists; refusing to overwrite trace evidence' >&2
+  exit 73
+fi
+for tool in strace readelf sha256sum timeout; do
+  if ! command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1; then

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Summarize completed strace calls; private arguments never enter public output.
+
+`-ff -ttt` prints one file per PID but may split an interrupted system call
+into `<unfinished ...>` and `<... syscall resumed>` lines. A half-call is
+NOT a completed syscall, and the errno belongs to the resumed half. Treat
+orphan/unfinished events as incomplete trace evidence rather than success.
+
+Do not equate syscall count/loader closure with authenticated Hepta tool effect.
+"""
+import argparse
+from collections import Counter
+import hashlib
+import json
+import os
+from pathlib import Path
+import re
+
+PREFIX = r"(?:\d+(?:\.\d+)?\s+)?"
+CALL = re.compile(r"^" + PREFIX + r"([a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*)\(")
+RESUME = re.compile(r"^" + PREFIX + r"<\.\.\. ([a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*) resumed>(.*)$")
+UNFINISHED = re.compile(r"\s+<unfinished \.\.\.>\s*$")
+RETURN = re.compile(r"\)\s+=\s+")
+ERR = re.compile(r"\)\s+=\s+-1\s+([A-Z][A-Z0-9_]+)(?:\s|$)")
+INTERNAL_RESTART = re.compile(r"\)\s+=\s+\?\s+(ERESTART[A-Z_]+)(?:\s|$)")
+QUOTED = re.compile(r'"((?:\\.|[^"\\])*)"')
+PROCESS_EXIT = re.compile(r"^" + PREFIX + r"\+\+\+ exited with (\d+) \+\+\+$")
+PROCESS_SIGNAL = re.compile(r"^" + PREFIX + r"\+\+\+ killed by (SIG[A-Z0-9]+)(?: \([^)]*\))? \+\+\+$")
+SHA_LINE = re.compile(r"^([0-9a-f]{64})  (.+)$")
+SIGNAL_NOTICE = re.compile(r"^" + PREFIX + r"--- SIG[A-Z0-9]+(?: .*?)? ---$")
+FILESYSTEM_CALLS = frozenset(("open", "openat", "openat2", "access", "faccessat",
+                              "faccessat2", "stat", "lstat", "newfstatat", "statx",
+                              "readlink", "readlinkat", "execve", "execveat"))
+
+
+def summarize(trace_dir, *, include_paths=False):
+    traces = sorted(p for p in trace_dir.glob("trace.*") if p.is_file() and
+                    re.fullmatch(r"trace\.\d+", p.name))
+    if not traces:
+        raise ValueError("zero real trace.PID logs; cannot report trace captured")
+    syscalls, errors, calls_by_error, paths, raw_files = Counter(), Counter(), Counter(), set(), []
+    restarts = Counter()
+    resumed_pairs = incomplete = orphan_resumptions = 0
+    terminated, missing_terminal, terminated_by_signal, unknown_lines = 0, 0, Counter(), 0
+    process_exit_codes = Counter()
+    observed_hashes = {}
+    for trace in traces:
+        sha = hashlib.sha256()
+        pending, terminal = None, False
+        with trace.open("rb") as stream:
+            for blob in stream:
+                sha.update(blob)
+                line = blob.decode("utf-8", "replace").rstrip("\r\n")
+                if not line:
+                    continue
+                if terminal:
+                    # Anything after +++ exited +++ means the trace is not a
+                    # trustworthy single-process lifecycle transcript.
+                    unknown_lines += 1
+                    continue
+                if (exited := PROCESS_EXIT.match(line)) is not None:
+                    process_exit_codes[exited.group(1)] += 1
+                    terminal = True
+                    terminated += 1
+                    continue
+                if (signaled := PROCESS_SIGNAL.match(line)) is not None:
+                    terminated_by_signal[signaled.group(1)] += 1
+                    terminal = True
+                    terminated += 1
+                    continue
+                if SIGNAL_NOTICE.match(line) or line.startswith("strace: Process "):
+                    continue
+                resumed = RESUME.match(line)
+                if resumed:
+                    syscall, tail = resumed.groups()
+                    if pending is None or pending[0] != syscall:
+                        orphan_resumptions += 1
+                        if pending is not None:
+                            incomplete += 1
+                        pending = None
+                        continue
+                    name, original = pending
+                    pending = None
+                    line = original + tail
+                    resumed_pairs += 1
+                else:
+                    match = CALL.match(line)
+                    if match is None:
+                        unknown_lines += 1
+                        continue
+                    syscall = match.group(1)
+                    if UNFINISHED.search(line):
+                        if pending is not None:
+                            incomplete += 1
+                        pending = (syscall, UNFINISHED.sub("", line))
+                        continue
+                    if pending is not None:
+                        # Trace may have been lost/truncated across the gap.
+                        incomplete += 1
+                        pending = None
+                match = CALL.match(line)
+                if not match or not RETURN.search(line):
+                    incomplete += 1
+                    continue
+                syscall = match.group(1)
+                if (restart := INTERNAL_RESTART.search(line)) is not None:
+                    # ERESTARTSYS and friends are kernel-internal; they are not
+                    # errno observed by user code, and completion is uncertain.
+                    restarts[f"{syscall}:{restart.group(1)}"] += 1
+                    incomplete += 1  # not yet a userspace-visible return
+                    continue
+                syscalls[syscall] += 1
+                if (error := ERR.search(line)) is not None:
+                    errors[error.group(1)] += 1
+                    calls_by_error[f"{syscall}:{error.group(1)}"] += 1
+                if include_paths and syscall in FILESYSTEM_CALLS:
+                    quoted = QUOTED.search(line[match.end():])
+                    if quoted:
+                        path = quoted.group(1)
+                        # Relative paths are not generally resolvable from a
+                        # strace log without a trustworthy per-process cwd.
+                        if path.startswith("/") and "\\" not in path and "\x00" not in path:
+                            paths.add(path)
+        if pending is not None:
+            incomplete += 1
+        if not terminal:
+            missing_terminal += 1
+        observed_hashes[trace.name] = sha.hexdigest()
+        raw_files.append({"sha256": sha.hexdigest(), "bytes": trace.stat().st_size})
+
+    # A completed syscall fragment is NOT evidence of a completed Agentd
+    # process tree. Require the actual strace -ff PID file manifest and the
+    # wrapper's exit status, in addition to every PID's terminal marker.
+    manifest_path = trace_dir / "trace-files.sha256"
+    integrity = "missing"
+    if manifest_path.is_file():
+        declared = {}
+        valid = True
+        for line in manifest_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
+            match = SHA_LINE.fullmatch(line)
+            if match is None:
+                valid = False
+                break
+            digest, filename = match.groups()
+            name = Path(filename).name
+            if (not re.fullmatch(r"trace\.\d+", name) or
+                    name in declared):
+                valid = False
+                break
+            declared[name] = digest
+        integrity = "verified" if valid and declared == observed_hashes else "mismatch"
+
+    tracer_status = None
+    tracer_exit_file = trace_dir / "exit-status.txt"
+    if tracer_exit_file.is_file():
+        contents = tracer_exit_file.read_text(encoding="ascii").strip()
+        if re.fullmatch(r"(?:0|[1-9]\d{0,2})", contents) and int(contents) <= 255:
+            tracer_status = int(contents)
+    finished = sum(syscalls.values())
+    if finished == 0:
+        raise ValueError("zero completed syscalls; no dependency closure was observed")
+    lifecycle_complete = (incomplete == orphan_resumptions == unknown_lines == missing_terminal == 0
+                          and not terminated_by_signal and terminated == len(traces)
+                          and integrity == "verified" and tracer_status == 0)
+    report = {"schema": 4, "kind": "aggregate_trace_only", "raw_trace_private": True,
+              "trace_file_count": len(raw_files), "raw_trace_hashes": raw_files,
+              "completed_syscalls": finished, "resumed_pairs": resumed_pairs,
+              "incomplete_syscalls": incomplete, "orphan_resumptions": orphan_resumptions,
+              "trace_completeness": "complete" if lifecycle_complete else "incomplete",
+              "trace_files_integrity": integrity, "strace_wrapper_exit_code": tracer_status,
+              "processes_with_terminal_marker": terminated,
+              "processes_missing_terminal_marker": missing_terminal,
+              "process_exit_status_counts": dict(sorted(process_exit_codes.items())),
+              "process_signal_termination_counts": dict(sorted(terminated_by_signal.items())),
+              "unrecognized_trace_lines": unknown_lines,
+              "kernel_internal_restarts": dict(sorted(restarts.items())),
+              "syscalls": dict(sorted(syscalls.items())), "errors": dict(sorted(errors.items())),
+              "syscall_errno": dict(sorted(calls_by_error.items())),
+              "path_values_excluded": True, "tool_execution_verified": False,
+              "hepta_e2e_verified": False,
+              "note": "Lifecycle completeness requires every PID exit, verified PID-log hashes and zero wrapper exit. Completed calls or successful ELF loading alone never prove W1 execution."}
+    return report, sorted(paths)
+
+
+def main():
+    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    ap.add_argument("trace_dir", type=Path)
+    ap.add_argument("--output", type=Path, required=True, help="safe aggregate counts only")
+    ap.add_argument("--private-path-output", type=Path,
+                    help="NEW local private candidate runtime-path inventory; NEVER commit")
+    args = ap.parse_args()
+    if args.output.exists() or (args.private_path_output and args.private_path_output.exists()):
+        ap.error("refusing to overwrite an existing trace report")
+    if args.private_path_output and args.output.resolve() == args.private_path_output.resolve():
+        ap.error("private paths must not share the public output file")
+    try:
+        report, paths = summarize(args.trace_dir, include_paths=args.private_path_output is not None)
+    except (ValueError, OSError) as e:
+        ap.exit(2, f"trace not obtained: {e}\n")
+    os.umask(0o077)
+    args.output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    args.output.write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
+    os.chmod(args.output, 0o600)
+    if args.private_path_output:
+        args.private_path_output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+        private = {"schema": 1, "kind": "PRIVATE_trace_paths_DO_NOT_COMMIT",
+                   "warning": "Paths may identify operators, user accounts or configuration; do not commit",
+                   "files": [{"path": p} for p in paths], "status": "candidate_only_unverified"}
+        args.private_path_output.write_text(json.dumps(private, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
+        os.chmod(args.private_path_output, 0o600)
+    print(f"{report['trace_file_count']} trace files; {report['completed_syscalls']} completed calls; "
+          f"lifecycle={report['trace_completeness']}; "
+          f"PID-log integrity={report['trace_files_integrity']}; "
+          f"private paths={len(paths)} (not in aggregate report); NO Hepta E2E claim")
+    # Do not let a truncated/timeout strace report turn a CI job green. The
+    # aggregate is still retained so the exact failure can be inspected.
+    return 0 if report['trace_completeness'] == 'complete' else 3
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())

+closure, plus glibc NSS modules, UTC, public CA trust, synthetic passwd/group,
+localhost and an intentionally unconfigured external resolver. It records every

+It never changes the system root, installs packages, invokes chroot, mounts or
+writes to production state. The generated `rootfs.tar` has sorted entries,
+uid/gid=0 and mtime=0, making it byte-stable for identical source bytes.

+mount. Host Python cases additionally need a separately pinned Python runtime

+reviewed resolver is part of the deployment profile.

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Capture an auditable *candidate* readonly Linux ELF rootfs without chroot/mount.
+
+The generated tar is deterministic for identical input bytes. This stages the
+ELF loader/DT_NEEDED closure, glibc NSS modules and public CA trust. Runtime
+dlopen, files, services and syscalls are NOT inferred from this static closure:
+only a real strace can qualify them, especially for the pinned Hepta profile.
+"""
+import argparse
+import hashlib
+import io
+import json
+import os
+from pathlib import Path, PurePosixPath
+import re
+import shutil
+import subprocess
+import tarfile
+
+
+def sha(path):
+    h = hashlib.sha256()
+    with open(path, "rb") as stream:
+        for chunk in iter(lambda: stream.read(1024 * 1024), b""):
+            h.update(chunk)
+    return h.hexdigest()
+
+
+def run(argv):
+    p = subprocess.run([str(x) for x in argv], capture_output=True, text=True)
+    if p.returncode:
+        raise RuntimeError(f"{' '.join(map(str, argv))}: {p.stderr.strip()}")
+    return p.stdout
+
+
+def elf_closure(elf):
+    headers = run(["readelf", "-l", elf])
+    needed = re.search(r"Requesting program interpreter: ([^]]+)", headers)
+    loader = needed.group(1) if needed else None
+    data = run(["readelf", "-d", elf])
+    dynamic_names = re.findall(r"Shared library: \[([^]]+)\]", data)
+    paths = set()
+    if loader:
+        paths.add(loader)
+        listing = run(["ldd", elf])  # Input MUST be a trusted, pinned ELF.
+        if "not found" in listing:
+            raise RuntimeError(f"unresolved DT_NEEDED for {elf}: {listing}")
+        paths.update(re.findall(r"(?:=>\s*)?(/[^\s(]+)\s*\(", listing))
+    return loader, dynamic_names, sorted(paths)
+
+
+def package(path):
+    candidates = [path]
+    if path.startswith("/lib/"):
+        candidates.append("/usr" + path)
+    if path.startswith("/lib64/"):
+        candidates.append("/usr" + path)
+    for candidate in candidates[::-1]:
+        p = subprocess.run(["dpkg-query", "-S", candidate], capture_output=True, text=True)
+        if p.returncode:
+            continue
+        first = next((x for x in p.stdout.splitlines() if ": " in x and not x.startswith("diversion ")), "")
+        if not first:
+            continue
+        owner = first.rsplit(": ", 1)[0].split(", ")[0]
+        v = subprocess.run(["dpkg-query", "-W", "-f=${Version}", owner], capture_output=True, text=True)
+        if v.returncode == 0:
+            return {"name": owner, "version": v.stdout.strip()}
+    return None
+
+
+def host_packages():
+    names = ("gcc", "libc6", "libc6-dev", "libsqlite3-0", "libsqlite3-dev",
+             "ca-certificates", "tzdata", "python3-minimal", "openssl")
+    installed = {}
+    for name in names:
+        p = subprocess.run(["dpkg-query", "-W", "-f=${Version}", name], capture_output=True, text=True)
+        if p.returncode == 0 and p.stdout.strip():
+            installed[name] = p.stdout.strip()
+    return installed
+
+
+def add_file(root, record, dest, source=None, data=None, executable=False):
+    if not dest.startswith("/") or ".." in Path(dest).parts or dest == "/":
+        raise ValueError("unsafe rootfs destination")
+    target = root / dest.lstrip("/")
+    target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    if target.exists():
+        raise ValueError(f"duplicate path: {dest}")
+    if source is not None:
+        if not Path(source).is_file():
+            raise FileNotFoundError(source)
+        target.write_bytes(Path(source).read_bytes())
+        origin = ({"build_source": "tests/workloads/linux/", "source_sha256": sha(source)}
+                  if dest.startswith("/usr/local/bin/a04/") else
+                  {"host_path": str(source), "source_sha256": sha(source), "package": package(str(source))})
+    else:
+        target.write_bytes(data)
+        origin = {"generated": True}
+    os.chmod(target, 0o555 if executable else 0o444)
+    record.append({"path": dest, "sha256": sha(target), "bytes": target.stat().st_size,
+                   "mode": "0555" if executable else "0444", "origin": origin})
+
+
+def create_tar(root, out):
+    """Deterministic USTAR with real DIRTYPE, never file-typed `etc/` entries.
+
+    tarfile.TarInfo(name + "/") does NOT set type=DIRTYPE automatically.
+    The old A04 archive therefore failed ordinary tarfile.extractall() at /etc.
+    Reject symlinks/special files so a staged rootfs cannot import host bytes.
+    """
+    root = Path(root)
+    with tarfile.open(out, "w", format=tarfile.USTAR_FORMAT) as tar:
+        files = sorted(root.rglob("*"), key=lambda x: x.relative_to(root).as_posix())
+        for file in files:
+            if file.is_symlink() or not (file.is_dir() or file.is_file()):
+                raise ValueError("unsupported staged rootfs entry: " + file.relative_to(root).as_posix())
+            is_dir = file.is_dir()
+            rel = file.relative_to(root).as_posix()
+            info = tarfile.TarInfo(rel + ("/" if is_dir else ""))
+            info.type = tarfile.DIRTYPE if is_dir else tarfile.REGTYPE
+            info.uid = info.gid = 0
+            info.uname = info.gname = ""
+            info.mtime = 0
+            info.mode = 0o755 if is_dir else file.stat().st_mode & 0o777
+            if is_dir:
+                info.size = 0
+                tar.addfile(info)
+            else:
+                content = file.read_bytes()
+                info.size = len(content)
+                tar.addfile(info, io.BytesIO(content))

+def extract_verified_tar(archive_path, manifest_path, destination):
+    """Materialize ONLY the manifest-pinned regular files in a fresh directory.
+
+    Refuse the old A04 archive with regular-file-typed directory entries,
+    links, path traversal, missing files or changed byte hashes. Never write
+    outside the new destination or silently relax pinned read-only modes.
+    This is host staging only, not a guest mounted-rootfs qualification.
+    """
+    destination = Path(destination)
+    if destination.exists() or destination.is_symlink():
+        raise ValueError("destination already exists; refusing extraction")
+    manifest = json.loads(Path(manifest_path).read_text())
+    expected = {}
+    for entry in manifest["files"]:
+        path = entry["path"]
+        if (not isinstance(path, str) or not path.startswith("/") or
+                path == "/" or PurePosixPath(path).as_posix() != path or
+                ".." in PurePosixPath(path).parts or path in expected):
+            raise ValueError("invalid or duplicate pinned manifest path")
+        expected[path[1:]] = entry
+    required_dirs = set()
+    for name in expected:
+        parent = PurePosixPath(name).parent
+        while str(parent) != ".":
+            required_dirs.add(str(parent))
+            parent = parent.parent
+    members = {}
+    with tarfile.open(archive_path, "r:") as tar:
+        for member in tar.getmembers():
+            name = member.name
+            path = PurePosixPath(name)
+            if (not name or path.is_absolute() or ".." in path.parts or
+                    path.as_posix() != name or name in members):
+                raise ValueError("unsafe or duplicate rootfs tar entry")
+            if member.isdir():
+                if name not in required_dirs or member.size != 0 or member.mode != 0o755:
+                    raise ValueError("unexpected rootfs directory or permissions")
+            elif member.isfile():
+                entry = expected.get(name)
+                if (entry is None or member.size != entry["bytes"] or
+                        member.mode != int(entry["mode"], 8)):
+                    raise ValueError("unexpected rootfs file, size or permissions")
+                handle = tar.extractfile(member)
+                if handle is None:
+                    raise ValueError("missing rootfs file data")
+                digest = hashlib.sha256()
+                for chunk in iter(lambda: handle.read(1024 * 1024), b""):
+                    digest.update(chunk)
+                if digest.hexdigest() != entry["sha256"]:
+                    raise ValueError("rootfs tar content SHA-256 mismatch")
+            else:
+                raise ValueError("rootfs tar contains link or special file")
+            members[name] = member
+        if (set(name for name, member in members.items() if member.isfile()) != set(expected)
+                or set(name for name, member in members.items() if member.isdir()) != required_dirs):
+            raise ValueError("rootfs tar file/directory closure differs from manifest")
+        destination.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+        destination.mkdir(mode=0o700)
+        for name in sorted(required_dirs, key=lambda x: (x.count("/"), x)):
+            (destination / name).mkdir(mode=0o755)
+        for name in sorted(expected):
+            target = destination / name
+            handle = tar.extractfile(members[name])
+            if handle is None:
+                raise ValueError("unexpected missing rootfs tar payload")
+            with target.open("xb") as dst:
+                shutil.copyfileobj(handle, dst, 1024 * 1024)
+            target.chmod(int(expected[name]["mode"], 8))
+    verify(destination, manifest_path)
+    return len(expected)
+
+
+def verify(root, manifest):
+    """Require an exact manifest of regular files; exclude symlink escape paths."""
+    root = Path(root)
+    obj = json.loads(Path(manifest).read_text())
+    records = obj["files"]
+    expected = {}
+    for record in records:
+        name = record["path"]
+        if (not isinstance(name, str) or not name.startswith("/")
+                or name == "/" or ".." in Path(name).parts or name in expected):
+            raise ValueError("invalid or duplicate rootfs manifest path")
+        expected[name] = (record["sha256"], record["mode"])
+    actual = {}
+    for entry in root.rglob("*"):
+        if entry.is_symlink() or not (entry.is_dir() or entry.is_file()):
+            raise ValueError("unsafe rootfs staging entry: " + entry.relative_to(root).as_posix())
+        if entry.is_file():
+            actual["/" + entry.relative_to(root).as_posix()] = (
+                sha(entry), f"{entry.stat().st_mode & 0o777:04o}")
+    if expected != actual:
+        missing = sorted(set(expected) - set(actual))
+        extra = sorted(set(actual) - set(expected))
+        mismatched = sorted(k for k in set(actual) & set(expected) if actual[k] != expected[k])
+        raise RuntimeError(f"rootfs changed: missing={missing}, extra={extra}, mismatch={mismatched}")
+    return len(actual)
+
+
+def main():
+    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
+    ap.add_argument("--root", type=Path, required=True, help="new rootfs directory")
+    ap.add_argument("--manifest", type=Path, required=True)
+    ap.add_argument("--tar", type=Path, help="optional deterministic uncompressed tar")
+    ap.add_argument("--binary", type=Path, action="append", help="trusted ELF to capture; repeat")
+    ap.add_argument("--verify", action="store_true", help="only check existing directory against manifest")
+    ap.add_argument("--extract-verified", action="store_true",
+                    help="extract an existing pinned --tar to NEW --root after strict verification")
+    args = ap.parse_args()
+    root = args.root.resolve()
+    if args.extract_verified:
+        if not args.tar or args.verify or args.binary:
+            ap.error("--extract-verified requires --tar and excludes --verify/--binary")
+        count = extract_verified_tar(args.tar, args.manifest, root)
+        print(json.dumps({"verified_extracted_files": count, "host_only": True}))
+        return
+    if args.verify:
+        print(json.dumps({"verified_files": verify(root, args.manifest)}))
+        return
+    if not args.binary:
+        ap.error("at least one --binary is required")
+    if root.exists():
+        ap.error("root already exists; refusing to overwrite")
+    root.mkdir(parents=True)
+    manifest = {"schema": 1, "kind": "candidate_elf_rootfs", "qualified_hepta": False,
+                "readonly_mount_verified": False,
+                "policy": {"rootfs": "read-only when mounted by guest; staging directory not a mounted filesystem",
+                           "writable_workspace": "/work (guest must mount separately)",
+                           "external_dns": "unconfigured", "timezone": "UTC", "locale": "C",
+                           "system_services": ["guest init", "procfs", "devtmpfs or /dev/null", "clock", "entropy"]},
+                "elf": [], "files": [], "host_packages": host_packages()}
+    files = manifest["files"]
+    libs = set()
+    for elf in args.binary:
+        path = elf.resolve()
+        loader, needed, paths = elf_closure(path)
+        dest = f"/usr/local/bin/a04/{path.name}"
+        add_file(root, files, dest, path, executable=True)
+        manifest["elf"].append({"name": path.name, "sha256": sha(path),
+                                "interpreter": loader, "needed": needed, "path": dest})
+        libs.update(paths)
+    # Glibc may dlopen these via NSS; ldd of the ELF alone cannot show them.
+    for nss in ("libnss_files.so.2", "libnss_dns.so.2"):
+        for base in ("/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu", "/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu"):
+            candidate = Path(base) / nss
+            if candidate.exists():
+                libs.add(str(candidate))
+                break
+    for lib in sorted(libs):
+        add_file(root, files, lib, lib, executable=True)
+    add_file(root, files, "/etc/nsswitch.conf",
+             data=b"passwd: files\ngroup: files\nhosts: files dns\n")
+    add_file(root, files, "/etc/hosts", data=b"127.0.0.1 localhost\n::1 localhost\n")
+    add_file(root, files, "/etc/passwd", data=b"root:x:0:0:root:/root:/bin/sh\nnobody:x:65534:65534:nobody:/:/usr/sbin/nologin\n")
+    add_file(root, files, "/etc/group", data=b"root:x:0:\nnogroup:x:65534:\n")
+    # No inherited host DNS settings, tokens, state, machine ID or SSH keys.
+    add_file(root, files, "/etc/resolv.conf", data=b"# no external DNS resolver pinned\n")
+    cert = Path("/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt")
+    if cert.is_file():
+        add_file(root, files, str(cert), cert)
+    zoneinfo = Path("/usr/share/zoneinfo/UTC")
+    if zoneinfo.is_file():
+        add_file(root, files, str(zoneinfo), zoneinfo)
+    files.sort(key=lambda item: item["path"])
+    args.manifest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    args.manifest.write_text(json.dumps(manifest, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
+    verified = verify(root, args.manifest)
+    tar_sha = None
+    if args.tar:
+        args.tar.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+        create_tar(root, args.tar)
+        tar_sha = sha(args.tar)
+    print(json.dumps({"verified_files": verified, "elf_count": len(manifest["elf"]),
+                      "tar_sha256": tar_sha, "hepta_qualified": False}))
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+# A04 Linux user ABI workloads — executable reference and guest replay
+
+Evidence is **real host Linux execution**, not a kernel compatibility claim.
+On Debian 13 x86_64 / Linux 6.18.44 / glibc 2.41 / GCC 14.2 /
+SQLite 3.46.1, 31/32 cases passed: 0 failed, 1 `not_run` (Rust/Tokio
+runtime blocked by managed-host pathname AF_UNIX `EPERM` after its reviewed
+locked build). 28/32 cases are the **same four C ELF** files and can run in
+A01's minimal initramfs without guest Python. Python SQLite/NSS/TLS (3) and
+Rust/Tokio (1) need independent guest runtime provisioning; they are never
+silently counted as passing.
+
+The independent Tokio workload now has a reviewed Cargo.lock with SHA-256
+`b38d7f2ae2d70dcd07bc58b5ecf050ae1d3ab19eb08acb4559f1a0c5929a1e42`. A locked
+release build under Rust 1.99.1 produced temporary ELF SHA-256
+`1b998b3f9bb144312dea4e75149dbf4d01819422421803f065c038666b36d8c5`.
+Runtime execution reached pathname AF_UNIX bind but the managed host returned
+`EPERM`; it remains unqualified and is not credited as a pass.
+
+The dedicated 2026-10-16 cloud preflight verified the A01 kernel/initramfs
+hashes but returned `blocked_environment_or_input` with exit 2 because QEMU was
+absent; its receipt remains historical evidence at
+`tests/workloads/linux/baselines/cloud-preflight-20261016.json`. A later
+non-system QEMU/SeaBIOS extraction booted the pinned A01 kernel/initramfs under
+TCG and exited 33; see `baselines/qemu-cloud-reprobe-20261017.json`.
+
+All host scratch writes are disposable; the C workloads compile both static
+and dynamic ELF and store exact SHA-256 / `PT_INTERP` / `DT_NEEDED` and
+observable state invariants. Only deterministic results are compared exactly.
+Build the same ELF bytes on the host, do **not** rebuild inside the guest.

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Validate the machine-readable A04 Linux workload contract.
+
+This module does not execute workloads.  It binds every observed case to the
+fixed Linux reference, records the argument vector and interface dependencies,
+and checks that release facts are present before a run can be reported.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import hashlib
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Any
+
+HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
+DEFAULT_CATALOG = HERE / "workload_catalog.json"
+DEFAULT_REFERENCE = HERE / "baselines/linux-debian13-x86_64.json"
+
+REQUIRED_INTERFACES = {
+    "auxv", "mmap", "pthread_create", "futex", "AF_UNIX", "epoll", "flock",
+    "fcntl_record_lock", "signal", "execve", "SQLite", "WAL", "eventfd",
+    "timerfd", "SCM_RIGHTS", "PTHREAD_MUTEX_ROBUST", "NSS", "TLS", "Rust",
+    "Tokio",
+}
+
+
+class CatalogError(ValueError):
+    """Raised when the catalog/reference contract is incomplete or unsafe."""
+
+
+def load_json(path: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    try:
+        value = json.loads(path.read_text())
+    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
+        raise CatalogError(f"cannot read JSON {path}: {exc}") from exc
+    if not isinstance(value, dict):
+        raise CatalogError(f"JSON root must be an object: {path}")
+    return value
+
+
+def sha256(path: Path) -> str:
+    digest = hashlib.sha256()
+    with path.open("rb") as stream:
+        for chunk in iter(lambda: stream.read(1024 * 1024), b""):
+            digest.update(chunk)
+    return digest.hexdigest()
+
+
+def _strings(value: Any, field: str, workload_id: str, *, nonempty: bool = True) -> list[str]:
+    if not isinstance(value, list) or (nonempty and not value) or not all(
+        isinstance(item, str) and item for item in value
+    ):
+        raise CatalogError(f"{workload_id}: {field} must be a string list")
+    return value
+
+
+def _string(value: Any, field: str, workload_id: str) -> str:
+    if not isinstance(value, str) or not value:
+        raise CatalogError(f"{workload_id}: {field} must be a non-empty string")
+    return value
+
+
+def validate(catalog: dict[str, Any], reference: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    if catalog.get("schema") != 1:
+        raise CatalogError("catalog schema must be 1")
+    reference_name = _string(catalog.get("reference"), "reference", "catalog")
+    if reference_name != "baselines/linux-debian13-x86_64.json":
+        raise CatalogError("catalog reference must bind the pinned Linux baseline")
+    workloads = catalog.get("workloads")
+    cases = reference.get("cases")
+    if not isinstance(workloads, list) or not workloads:
+        raise CatalogError("catalog workloads must be a non-empty list")
+    if not isinstance(cases, dict) or not cases:
+        raise CatalogError("reference cases must be a non-empty object")
+    seen: set[str] = set()
+    interfaces: set[str] = set()
+    by_class: dict[str, int] = {}
+    for item in workloads:
+        if not isinstance(item, dict):
+            raise CatalogError("workload entries must be objects")
+        workload_id = item.get("id")
+        if not isinstance(workload_id, str) or not workload_id:
+            raise CatalogError("workload id must be a non-empty string")
+        if workload_id in seen:
+            raise CatalogError(f"duplicate workload id: {workload_id}")
+        seen.add(workload_id)
+        if workload_id not in cases:
+            raise CatalogError(f"{workload_id}: missing from Linux reference")
+        workload_class = item.get("class")
+        if workload_class not in {"elf", "python", "rust"}:
+            raise CatalogError(f"{workload_id}: unsupported class {workload_class!r}")
+        by_class[workload_class] = by_class.get(workload_class, 0) + 1
+        if not isinstance(item.get("operation"), str) or not item["operation"]:
+            raise CatalogError(f"{workload_id}: operation is required")
+        _strings(item.get("command"), "command", workload_id)
+        _strings(item.get("inputs"), "inputs", workload_id)
+        item_interfaces = _strings(item.get("interfaces"), "interfaces", workload_id)
+        interfaces.update(item_interfaces)
+        release_keys = _strings(item.get("release_fact_keys"), "release_fact_keys", workload_id,
+                                nonempty=False)
+        expected = cases[workload_id]
+        status = expected.get("status")
+        if status not in {"pass", "fail", "not_run"}:
+            raise CatalogError(f"{workload_id}: invalid reference status {status!r}")
+        if status == "pass":
+            facts = expected.get("facts")
+            if not isinstance(facts, dict) or facts.get("ok") is not True:
+                raise CatalogError(f"{workload_id}: passing reference lacks ok=true facts")
+            missing = [key for key in release_keys if key not in facts]
+            if missing:
+                raise CatalogError(f"{workload_id}: release facts missing {missing}")
+        elif workload_class == "rust" and not item.get("qualification_blocker"):
+            raise CatalogError(f"{workload_id}: not-run Rust entry needs a blocker")
+    missing_cases = sorted(set(cases) - seen)
+    if missing_cases:
+        raise CatalogError(f"catalog omits reference cases: {missing_cases}")
+    missing_interfaces = sorted(REQUIRED_INTERFACES - interfaces)
+    if missing_interfaces:
+        raise CatalogError(f"catalog omits required interfaces: {missing_interfaces}")
+    counts = {state: sum(value.get("status") == state for value in cases.values())
+              for state in ("pass", "fail", "not_run")}
+    return {
+        "schema": 1,
+        "profile": catalog.get("profile"),
+        "catalog_workload_count": len(seen),
+        "reference_case_count": len(cases),
+        "reference_counts": counts,
+        "workloads_by_class": dict(sorted(by_class.items())),
+        "interfaces": sorted(interfaces),
+        "required_interfaces": sorted(REQUIRED_INTERFACES),
+    }
+
+
+def validate_files(catalog_path: Path = DEFAULT_CATALOG,
+                   reference_path: Path = DEFAULT_REFERENCE) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    summary = validate(load_json(catalog_path), load_json(reference_path))
+    summary.update({"catalog_sha256": sha256(catalog_path),
+                    "reference_sha256": sha256(reference_path)})
+    return summary
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--catalog", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_CATALOG)
+    parser.add_argument("--reference", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_REFERENCE)
+    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path)
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    try:
+        summary = validate_files(args.catalog, args.reference)
+    except CatalogError as exc:
+        parser.error(str(exc))
+    text = json.dumps(summary, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n"
+    if args.output:
+        if args.output.exists() or args.output.is_symlink():
+            parser.error(f"refusing to overwrite {args.output}")
+        args.output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+        args.output.write_text(text)
+    print(json.dumps({key: summary[key] for key in
+                      ("catalog_sha256", "reference_sha256", "catalog_workload_count",
+                       "reference_counts")}, sort_keys=True))
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Execute fixed A04 C ELF inside a strictly extracted rootfs on ORIGINAL Linux.
+
+Distinct from staged loader execution: chroot resolves PT_INTERP, all DT_NEEDED
+libraries and runtime file lookups inside the 17-file captured rootfs. The
+child drops to uid/gid 65534; the only writable area is /tmp/a04/CASE.
+No mounts, containers, package installs, privileged guest or system disk
+changes. chroot is NOT a network/PID/user namespace sandbox, not Asterinas,
+not Hepta W1 and not an S1 persistence qualification.
+"""
+import argparse
+import hashlib
+import importlib.util
+import json
+import os
+from pathlib import Path
+import platform
+import signal
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import tempfile
+
+HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
+ROOT = HERE.parents[2]
+
+
+def module(name, source):
+    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name, source)
+    value = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
+    spec.loader.exec_module(value)
+    return value
+
+
+capture = module('a04_chroot_capture', ROOT/'support/rootfs/capture.py')
+guest = module('a04_chroot_guest', HERE/'guest.py')
+
+
+def enter_chroot(root):
+    # preexec_fn executes only in forked child, before execve. Parent never chroots.
+    os.chroot(root)
+    os.chdir('/')
+    os.setgroups([])
+    os.setgid(65534)
+    os.setuid(65534)
+
+
+def bounded_run(command, *, env, timeout, preexec_fn):
+    """Kill the entire disposable process group, not just a timed-out parent.
+
+    A forked descendant can inherit stdout/stderr and keep communicate() open
+    after a parent exits. Returning before all pipe owners have died would
+    also invalidate file-lock and resource-release observations.
+    """
+    proc = subprocess.Popen(command, cwd='/', env=env, stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
+                            stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True,
+                            start_new_session=True, preexec_fn=preexec_fn)
+    stdout, stderr, timed_out, cleanup_incomplete = '', '', False, False
+    try:
+        stdout, stderr = proc.communicate(timeout=timeout)
+    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
+        timed_out = True
+    finally:
+        try:
+            os.killpg(proc.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
+        except ProcessLookupError:
+            pass
+        if proc.poll() is None:
+            proc.kill()
+        try:
+            # After killing the whole group, all inherited pipes must close.
+            proc.communicate(timeout=3)
+        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
+            # A grandchild may have called setsid() and escaped the original
+            # process group while retaining a pipe. Never wait forever or
+            # claim its cleanup was verified.
+            cleanup_incomplete = True
+            for pipe in (proc.stdout, proc.stderr):
+                if pipe is not None:
+                    pipe.close()
+            proc.wait(timeout=3)
+    return {'exit_code': proc.returncode, 'stdout': stdout, 'stderr': stderr,
+            'timed_out': timed_out, 'cleanup_incomplete': cleanup_incomplete}
+
+
+def exact_observation(execution, reference_case):
+    """Fail closed for stderr, extra output, ambiguous JSON and exit drift.
+
+    The same rule must be used by one-shot chroot and repeated chroot stress.
+    The guest serial parser independently enforces this contract.
+    """
+    if execution.get('timed_out'):
+        return None, False, 'timeout_descendants_terminated'
+    if execution.get('cleanup_incomplete'):
+        return None, False, 'incomplete_descendant_cleanup'
+    if execution.get('exit_code') != reference_case.get('exit_code'):
+        return None, False, 'exit_code_mismatch'
+    if execution.get('stderr'):
+        return None, False, 'unexpected_stderr'
+    stdout = execution.get('stdout')
+    if not isinstance(stdout, str) or len(stdout.splitlines()) != 1:
+        return None, False, 'unexpected_stdout'
+    try:
+        facts = guest._json_unique_guest_object(stdout)
+    except (json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError):
+        return None, False, 'invalid_or_ambiguous_json'
+    if not isinstance(facts, dict) or facts != reference_case.get('facts') or facts.get('ok') is not True:
+        return facts, False, 'observable_result_mismatch'
+    return facts, True, None
+
+
+def run(tar_path, manifest_path, reference, *, timeout=30):
+    if platform.system() != 'Linux' or platform.machine() != 'x86_64':
+        raise ValueError('x86_64 original Linux required')
+    if os.geteuid() != 0:
+        raise PermissionError('CAP_SYS_CHROOT/root required in disposable test host')
+    if timeout < 1 or timeout > 60:
+        raise ValueError('timeout must be in 1..60 seconds')
+    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='a04-chroot-replay-') as work:
+        root = Path(work)/'root'
+        captured_count = capture.extract_verified_tar(tar_path, manifest_path, root)
+        # This is a writable ephemeral COPY. The manifest-pinned source tree and
+        # read-only file modes are unchanged; no host mount table is altered.
+        root.chmod(0o755)
+        (root/'tmp').mkdir(mode=0o1777)
+        (root/'tmp').chmod(0o1777)
+        (root/'tmp/a04').mkdir(mode=0o711)
+        (root/'tmp/a04').chmod(0o711)
+        manifest = json.loads(Path(manifest_path).read_text())
+        pinned = guest.verify_binary_identity(root, manifest, reference,
+                                              required_stems=reference['binaries'])
+        cases = {}
+        for name, stem, case in guest.reference_elf_cases(reference):
+            binary = pinned[guest.BINARY_FOR[stem]]
+            if binary['sha256'] != reference['binaries'][stem]['sha256']:
+                raise ValueError('ELF manifest SHA diverges from Linux reference')
+            scratch = '/tmp/a04/' + name
+            case_dir = root / scratch.lstrip('/')
+            case_dir.mkdir(mode=0o700)
+            os.chown(case_dir, 65534, 65534)
+            exe = binary['path']
+            command = [exe] + ([scratch] if stem.startswith('sqlite_') else [case, scratch])
+            # Fixed process environment, NO host LD_LIBRARY_PATH/preloads,
+            # credentials, host paths or provider configuration inherited.
+            env = {'PATH': '/usr/local/bin/a04', 'LC_ALL': 'C', 'TZ': 'UTC',
+                   'HOME': scratch}
+            try:
+                execution = bounded_run(command, env=env, timeout=timeout,
+                                        preexec_fn=lambda: enter_chroot(root))
+                facts, success, error = exact_observation(execution, reference['cases'][name])
+                cases[name] = {'status': 'pass' if success else 'fail',
+                               'exit_code': execution['exit_code'], 'facts': facts,
+                               'error': error,
+                               'scratch': 'volatile_chroot'}
+            except (OSError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired, ValueError) as exc:
+                cases[name] = {'status': 'fail', 'exit_code': None, 'facts': None,
+                               'error': type(exc).__name__, 'scratch': 'volatile_chroot'}
+        for name in reference['cases']:
+            if name not in cases:
+                cases[name] = {'status': 'not_run', 'reason': 'requires Python or Rust guest runtime'}
+        counts = {status: sum(1 for entry in cases.values() if entry['status'] == status)
+                  for status in ('pass', 'fail', 'not_run')}
+        return {'schema': 1, 'suite': 'a04-host-linux-chroot-elf-only',
+                'platform': {'system': platform.system(), 'machine': platform.machine(),
+                             'release': platform.release(), 'execution': 'host_linux_chroot_uid65534',
+                             'mounts_changed': False, 'network_namespace_isolated': False},
+                'binaries': reference['binaries'], 'cases': dict(sorted(cases.items())),
+                'counts': counts, 'rootfs_manifest_sha256': capture.sha(manifest_path),
+                'rootfs_tar_sha256': capture.sha(tar_path), 'manifest_files_verified': captured_count,
+                'rootfs_fully_isolated_from_host_loader': True,
+                'kernel_guest_verified': False, 'guest_execution_verified': False,
+                'real_hepta_w1_verified': False, 's1_storage_verified': False}
+
+
+def main():
+    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    ap.add_argument('--tar', type=Path, required=True, help='fixed corrected rootfs USTAR')
+    ap.add_argument('--manifest', type=Path, required=True)
+    ap.add_argument('--reference', type=Path, required=True)
+    ap.add_argument('--output', type=Path, required=True)
+    ap.add_argument('--timeout', type=int, default=30)
+    args = ap.parse_args()
+    if args.output.exists() or args.output.is_symlink():
+        ap.error('refusing to overwrite existing evidence')
+    try:
+        reference = json.loads(args.reference.read_text())
+        result = run(args.tar.resolve(), args.manifest.resolve(),
+                     reference, timeout=args.timeout)
+    except (OSError, RuntimeError, ValueError, KeyError, json.JSONDecodeError, EOFError) as exc:
+        ap.exit(2, 'A04 host chroot baseline blocked: ' + type(exc).__name__ + ': ' + str(exc) + '\n')
+    args.output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    args.output.write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + '\n')
+    print(json.dumps({'counts': result['counts'], 'rootfs_verified_files': result['manifest_files_verified'],
+                      'kernel_guest_verified': False}))
+    expected_c = len(guest.reference_elf_cases(reference))
+    expected_skipped = len(reference["cases"]) - expected_c
+    return 0 if result["counts"] == {"pass": expected_c, "fail": 0,
+                                      "not_run": expected_skipped} else 1
+
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+    sys.exit(main())

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Repeated ORIGINAL Linux chroot stress for the same pinned A04 application probes.
+
+This is not Asterinas, Hepta, CPU scheduling qualification or an S1 crash test.
+Only synthetic /tmp test directories are writable. The fixed 17-file rootfs
+is verified and extracted to a disposable location, then each child drops to
+uid/gid 65534. A failing case or timeout is preserved as a failure, never a
+skip or ABI diagnosis. Per-case assertions compare complete observable facts.
+"""
+import argparse
+import hashlib
+import importlib.util
+import json
+import os
+from pathlib import Path
+import platform
+# Process-group timeout cleanup is centralized in chroot.bounded_run.
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import tempfile
+
+HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
+ROOT = HERE.parents[2]
+
+
+def load(name, path):
+    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name, path)
+    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
+    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
+    return module
+
+
+capture = load('a04_stress_capture', ROOT / 'support/rootfs/capture.py')
+chroot = load('a04_stress_chroot', HERE / 'chroot_replay.py')
+guest = load('a04_stress_guest', HERE / 'guest.py')
+
+STRESS_KINDS = frozenset(('threads_futex', 'async_fd', 'robust_owner_death',
+                          'uds_peercred', 'scm_rights', 'file_lock', 'process',
+                          'mmap_cow', 'sqlite_wal_elf'))
+
+

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Run A04's exact guest-run.sh under the ORIGINAL Linux kernel in a chroot.
+
+This validates the *guest script and the real pinned ELF/loader/SQLite files*,
+not Asterinas/QEMU compatibility. No disk mounts, network or production
+services are touched. The only unpinned, ephemeral host additions are BusyBox
+and its loader dependencies; those are recorded independently in the result.
+"""
+import argparse
+import hashlib
+import importlib.util
+import json
+import os
+from pathlib import Path
+import platform
+import re
+import signal
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import tempfile
+
+HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
+ROOT = HERE.parents[2]
+
+
+def import_from(name, path):
+    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name, path)
+    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
+    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
+    return module
+
+
+guest = import_from("a04_shell_guest", HERE / "guest.py")
+capture = import_from("a04_shell_capture", ROOT / "support/rootfs/capture.py")
+
+
+def busybox_dependencies(path):
+    """Only inspect the explicitly supplied, trusted host BusyBox binary."""
+    p = subprocess.run(["ldd", str(path)], capture_output=True, text=True,
+                       check=False, timeout=10)
+    if p.returncode != 0 and "not a dynamic executable" not in (p.stdout + p.stderr):
+        raise ValueError("ldd could not classify trusted BusyBox dependencies")
+    if "not found" in p.stdout:
+        raise ValueError("host BusyBox has unresolved dependencies")
+    return sorted(set(re.findall(r"(?:=>\s*)?(/[\w+.,@/-]+)\s*\(", p.stdout)))
+
+
+def stage_busybox(root, busybox):
+    """Never modify manifest-pinned ELF/rootfs files; track all host additions."""
+    if not busybox.is_file():
+        raise ValueError("trusted BusyBox input is absent")
+    included = {}
+    sources = [("/bin/busybox", busybox)]
+    sources.extend((path, Path(path)) for path in busybox_dependencies(busybox))
+    for rel, source in sources:
+        if not source.is_file() or not rel.startswith(("/bin/", "/lib/", "/lib64/", "/usr/lib/")):
+            raise ValueError("unsupported BusyBox runtime dependency")
+        dest = root / rel.lstrip("/")
+        if dest.exists():
+            if guest.sha_file(dest) != guest.sha_file(source):
+                raise ValueError("BusyBox dependency differs from pinned rootfs library")
+            continue
+        dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+        dest.write_bytes(source.read_bytes())
+        dest.chmod(0o555)
+        included[rel] = guest.sha_file(dest)
+    sh = root / "bin/sh"
+    if sh.exists() or sh.is_symlink():
+        raise ValueError("untrusted /bin/sh already exists in the rootfs overlay")
+    sh.symlink_to("busybox")
+    return included
+
+
+def enter_chroot(root):
+    # Dedicated process group permits bounded cleanup of grandchildren.
+    os.setsid()
+    os.chroot(root)
+    os.chdir("/")
+    os.setgroups([])
+    os.setgid(65534)
+    os.setuid(65534)
+
+
+def evaluate_output(stdout, exit_code, reference):
+    """Exercise the actual guest serial parser without asserting a QEMU boot."""
+    rc = 0 if exit_code == 0 else 1
+    # Explicitly SYNTHETIC envelope: the original-Linux host output never
+    # provides A01 kernel / QEMU evidence and cannot qualify a guest boot.
+    serial = ("TRILLIONNIUM_A01_INIT_BEGIN\nTRILLIONNIUM_A01_BOOT_OK\n"
+              "TRILLIONNIUM_A04_WORKLOAD_BEGIN\n" + stdout +
+              f"TRILLIONNIUM_A04_RUNNER_STATUS={rc}\n"
+              "TRILLIONNIUM_A04_WORKLOAD_END\n")
+    names = [name for name, _, _ in guest.reference_elf_cases(reference)]
+    report = guest.parse_serial(serial, reference,
+                                {"cases": names, "a04_initramfs_sha256": "HOST_ONLY"},
+                                qemu_exit=None, kernel_sha=None, image_sha=None)
+    if report["guest_execution_verified"] or report["guest_compatibility_passed"]:
+        raise RuntimeError("host shell replay was incorrectly accepted as a kernel guest")
+    expected_skips = len(reference["cases"]) - len(names)
+    passed = (exit_code == 0 and report["counts"] ==
+              {"pass": len(names), "fail": 0, "not_run": expected_skips}
+              and not report["boot_evidence"]["anomalies"])
+    return passed, report
+
+
+def run(rootfs_tar, manifest, reference, busybox, *, timeout=120):
+    if platform.system() != "Linux" or platform.machine() != "x86_64":
+        raise ValueError("original x86_64 Linux host required")
+    if os.geteuid() != 0:
+        raise PermissionError("chroot requires root/CAP_SYS_CHROOT in a disposable environment")
+    if not 5 <= timeout <= 600:
+        raise ValueError("timeout must be in 5..600 seconds")
+    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="a04-shell-rehearsal-") as tmp:
+        root = Path(tmp) / "root"
+        files_verified = capture.extract_verified_tar(rootfs_tar, manifest, root)
+        additions = stage_busybox(root, busybox)
+        root.chmod(0o755)
+        writable = root / "tmp"
+        writable.mkdir(mode=0o1777)
+        writable.chmod(0o1777)
+        script = root / "test/a04/guest-run.sh"
+        script.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+        script.write_bytes(guest.make_guest_script(guest.reference_elf_cases(reference)))
+        script.chmod(0o555)
+        env = {"PATH": "/bin:/usr/local/bin/a04", "LC_ALL": "C", "TZ": "UTC",
+               "HOME": "/tmp"}
+        proc = subprocess.Popen(["/bin/busybox", "sh", "/test/a04/guest-run.sh"],
+                                cwd="/", env=env, stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
+                                stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True,
+                                preexec_fn=lambda: enter_chroot(root))
+        timed_out = False
+        try:
+            stdout, stderr = proc.communicate(timeout=timeout)
+        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
+            # Shell-run probes can spawn grandchildren. Killing only the shell
+            # would leave orphan C ELF tasks and file-lock holders behind.
+            timed_out = True
+            os.killpg(proc.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
+            stdout, stderr = proc.communicate(timeout=10)
+        passed, facts = evaluate_output(stdout, proc.returncode, reference)
+        return {"schema": 1, "kind": "a04_original_linux_chroot_guest_shell_rehearsal",
+                "passed": passed and not timed_out, "exit_code": proc.returncode,
+                "timed_out": timed_out,
+                "stdout_sha256": hashlib.sha256(stdout.encode()).hexdigest(),
+                "stderr_sha256": hashlib.sha256(stderr.encode()).hexdigest(),
+                "rootfs_tar_sha256": guest.sha_file(rootfs_tar),
+                "rootfs_manifest_sha256": guest.sha_file(manifest),
+                "files_verified": files_verified,
+                "host_busybox_sha256": guest.sha_file(busybox),
+                "host_only_runtime_additions": additions,
+                "counts": facts["counts"],
+                "parser_anomalies": facts["boot_evidence"]["anomalies"],
+                "qemu_used": False, "guest_execution_verified": False,
+                "hepta_w1_verified": False, "writable_area": "disposable_chroot_directory_not_tmpfs"}
+
+
+def main():
+    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    ap.add_argument("--tar", type=Path, required=True)
+    ap.add_argument("--manifest", type=Path, required=True)
+    ap.add_argument("--reference", type=Path, required=True)
+    ap.add_argument("--busybox", type=Path, default=Path("/usr/bin/busybox"))
+    ap.add_argument("--output", type=Path, required=True)
+    ap.add_argument("--timeout", type=int, default=120)
+    args = ap.parse_args()
+    if args.output.exists() or args.output.is_symlink():
+        ap.error("refusing to overwrite previous evidence")
+    try:
+        baseline = json.loads(args.reference.read_text())
+        result = run(args.tar, args.manifest, baseline, args.busybox, timeout=args.timeout)
+        result["linux_reference_sha256"] = guest.sha_file(args.reference)
+    except (OSError, ValueError, RuntimeError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired,
+            json.JSONDecodeError, KeyError) as exc:
+        ap.exit(2, f"A04 original Linux guest script rehearsal blocked: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}\n")
+    args.output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    args.output.write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
+    print(json.dumps({"kind": result["kind"], "passed": result["passed"],
+                      "counts": result["counts"], "qemu_used": False}))
+    return 0 if result["passed"] else 1
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main())

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Trace pinned *host Linux* A04 ELF cases using argument-free ptrace.
+
+Unlike strace, the fallback records syscall number/errno (no paths/arguments).
+The raw JSONL stays PRIVATE; the public aggregate retains counts, evidence
+hashes and deterministic application observations. Neither means Hepta W1, A01
+kernel testing, actual rootfs isolation or full dynamic dependency closure.
+"""
+import argparse
+from collections import Counter
+import errno
+import hashlib
+import importlib.util
+import json
+import os
+from pathlib import Path
+import platform
+import re
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import tempfile
+
+HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
+ROOT = HERE.parents[2]
+
+
+def imported(name, path):
+    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name, path)
+    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
+    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
+    return module
+
+
+runner = imported("a04_ptrace_runner", HERE / "run.py")
+guest = imported("a04_ptrace_guest", HERE / "guest.py")
+capture = imported("a04_ptrace_capture", ROOT / "support/rootfs/capture.py")
+
+
+def syscall_numbers(header):
+    pattern = re.compile(r"^#define\s+__NR_([A-Za-z0-9_]+)\s+(\d+)\s*$", re.M)
+    names = {int(number): name for name, number in pattern.findall(header.read_text())}
+    if not names or names.get(0) != "read":
+        raise ValueError("incorrect Linux x86_64 syscall number table")
+    return names
+
+
+def inspect_trace(path):
+    if not path.is_file() or path.stat().st_size == 0:
+        raise ValueError("trace log missing or empty")
+    total = 0
+    syscalls = Counter()
+    errors = Counter()
+    restarts = Counter()
+    tids = set()
+    exits = 0
+    with path.open("rb") as trace:
+        for blob in trace:
+            row = json.loads(blob)
+            if not isinstance(row, dict) or type(row.get("tid")) is not int or row["tid"] <= 0:
+                raise ValueError("invalid trace event identity")
+            tids.add(row["tid"])
+            kind = row.get("kind")
+            if kind == "syscall":
+                nr, error = row.get("nr"), row.get("errno")
+                internal_restart = row.get("internal_restart", 0)
+                if type(internal_restart) is not int or internal_restart not in (0, 512, 513, 514, 515, 516):
+                    raise ValueError("invalid kernel-internal restart")
+                if error and internal_restart:
+                    raise ValueError("internal restart cannot be reported as userspace errno")
+                if type(nr) is not int or nr < 0 or type(error) is not int or error < 0 or error > 4095 or 512 <= error <= 516:
+                    raise ValueError("invalid trace syscall number or errno")
+                syscalls[nr] += 1
+                if error:
+                    errors[(nr, error)] += 1
+                if internal_restart:
+                    restarts[(nr, internal_restart)] += 1
+                total += 1
+            elif kind == "exit":
+                if type(row.get("code")) is not int or row["code"] < 0 or row["code"] > 255:
+                    raise ValueError("invalid process exit")
+                exits += 1
+            else:
+                raise ValueError("unknown trace event")
+    if total == 0 or exits == 0:
+        raise ValueError("incomplete trace: no syscall completion or process exit")
+    return {"syscall_events": total, "process_or_thread_exits": exits,
+            "observed_threads": len(tids), "syscalls": syscalls,
+            "syscall_errno": errors, "internal_restarts": restarts,
+            "sha256": runner.digest(path), "bytes": path.stat().st_size}
+
+
+def compile_tracer(output):
+    command = ["gcc", "-O2", "-std=c11", "-Wall", "-Wextra", "-Werror",
+               str(HERE / "ptrace_trace.c"), "-o", str(output)]
+    p = subprocess.run(command, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=60, check=False)
+    if p.returncode:
+        raise RuntimeError(f"ptrace tracer compile failed: {p.stderr[-1200:]}")
+    return runner.digest(output)
+
+
+def run(reference, rootfs, manifest_path, out, trace_dir, header):
+    if platform.system() != "Linux" or platform.machine() != "x86_64":
+        raise ValueError("x86_64 Linux ptrace baseline required")
+    if trace_dir.exists() or trace_dir.is_symlink():
+        raise ValueError("private trace dir already exists: refusing overwrite")
+    if out.exists():
+        raise ValueError("aggregate output already exists: refusing overwrite")
+    capture.verify(rootfs, manifest_path)
+    fixed_manifest = json.loads(manifest_path.read_text())
+    pinned = {x["name"]: x for x in fixed_manifest["elf"]}
+    names = syscall_numbers(header)
+    os.umask(0o077)
+    trace_dir.mkdir(parents=True, mode=0o700)
+    trace_dir.chmod(0o700)
+    cases = {}
+    errors = Counter()
+    restarts = Counter()
+    observed = Counter()
+    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="a04-ptrace-work-") as scratch_dir:
+        scratch = Path(scratch_dir)
+        tracer = scratch / "a04-ptrace"
+        tracer_sha = compile_tracer(tracer)
+        env = os.environ.copy()

+            if actual_sha != elf["sha256"] or actual_sha != reference["binaries"][stem]["sha256"]:

+            interp = reference["binaries"][stem]["interpreter"]
+            command = [binary] if not interp else [rootfs / interp.lstrip("/"),
+                          "--library-path", rootfs / "lib/x86_64-linux-gnu", binary]
+            case_dir = scratch / name
+            case_dir.mkdir()
+            command += [case_dir] if stem.startswith("sqlite_") else [case, case_dir]
+            raw_path = trace_dir / (name + ".jsonl")
+            try:
+                proc = subprocess.run([str(tracer), str(raw_path), "--", *map(str, command)],
+                                      cwd=case_dir, env=env, capture_output=True,
+                                      text=True, timeout=45, check=False)
